title: Trump Ends Canada Trade Talks and Announces a 10% Tariff Increase Over Ontario’s Reagan Ad
description_short: Trump said he was ending trade talks with Canada over Ontario’s Reagan ad and announced an additional 10% tariff, without specifying affected goods.
description_medium: On Oct. 23, 2025, Trump called Ontario’s Reagan ad “FAKE” and said he was ending trade negotiations with Canada. The next day, he suggested to reporters that the ad might have used AI, a claim not established by the sources. On Oct. 25, he announced an additional 10% tariff on Canada over the ad; Reuters reported that the affected goods were not specified.
description_long: Ontario’s provincial government aired a television advertisement using excerpts from former President Ronald Reagan’s 1987 radio address about tariffs. FactCheck.org found that the ad rearranged parts of the address and omitted context, but did not change Reagan’s broader anti-tariff message. On Oct. 23, 2025, Trump called the ad “FAKE,” said it was intended to interfere with pending Supreme Court tariff litigation, and announced that he was ending trade negotiations with Canada. The following day, he told reporters, “I guess it was AI or something”; this was an attributed suggestion, not evidence about how the advertisement was produced. On Oct. 25, Trump announced an additional 10% tariff on Canada, citing the ad. Reuters reported that he did not specify which goods the increase would cover and that most Canadian exports were exempt from tariffs under USMCA. Ontario Premier Doug Ford had said the province would pause the U.S. ad campaign on Monday after discussions with Prime Minister Mark Carney so trade talks could resume. This proposal records Trump’s announced actions and stated reasons; it does not say the tariff took effect or establish the later course of negotiations.
